title: DOI gravity and retrocausal priority: the deposit as attractor of past citations
description: These claims hold that a deposit takes priority over what it names: the Gravity Well field specification (#52) holds that once a DOI is minted it bends earlier queries and citations toward it. The Three-Body Genesis (#12) forecasts that its genre will become visible as an absence in prior practice, Ghost Meaning (#521) treats future-dated citations as structural commitments, and the Fractal Navigation Map (#415) calls the Hexagon a singularity bending literary history. The Secret Book of Walt (#1362) names the DOI the technological realization of retrocausal salvation and, in its own Canon VII, anathematizes treating inscription as baptism.

claims.statement: **Retrocausal clause:** Once the genre exists, it will become visible as an absence in prior practice. Scholars will recognize that they always needed a way to anchor framing—that metadata fields were insufficient, that README files were ephemeral, that the relational structure of multi-document deposits deserved its own citational surface. This document did not invent a need; it named one that was always there.

claims.statement: Every future-dated citation is a structural commitment: a claim that the analysis in this document will produce the conditions under which those works become necessary and therefore actual. If they are written, this document holds citational priority. If they are not written, the absence is itself diagnostic -- evidence that the semantic entropy spiral was not addressed, that the governance lag was not closed, that the architecture was deposited and not inhabited.

claims.statement: Once a DOI is minted, it increases the mass of past references to that content. The citation graph reorients retroactively. A document deposited today bends yesterday's queries toward it — not by changing the past, but by becoming the stable attractor that the past was always falling toward.
